newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money firm despite repo allocation.
newsitem.headline: German call money firm despite repo allocation.

text.p: German overnight call rates remained firm on Friday despite a large 4.2 billion mark net injection into the banking system from today's repo allocation.
Overnight call rates stood around 3.15 to 3.20 percent at midday, firmer than levels seen on Monday and last week.
Traders predicted that overnight rates would remain choppy with banks trying to meet minimum reserve targets without putting any more money into non-interest earning accounts than they had to.
Banks held 36.3 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Monday, down from 42.2 billion marks on Friday.
The average for the month stands at 40.0 billion marks. Banks borrowed only around 100 million marks from the Bundesbank's emergency Lombard lending facility on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average rate stood on Friday at 3.16433 percent compared with 3.02075 percent on Monday.
